items.primary_i_can: I can recognize static equilibrium and dynamic equilibrium.
items.source_basis: Original Unit 1 Assessment Plan §1.4: static/dynamic equilibrium, forces at rest, ΣF=0 for constant straight-line motion; Physics Framework: balanced-force model reasoning.
items.student_text: A drone hovers motionless with balanced forces. A train moves straight at constant speed with balanced forces. Which classification is correct?
items.student_html: A drone hovers motionless with balanced forces. A train moves straight at constant speed with balanced forces. Which classification is correct?
items.solution_text: Rest with zero net force is static equilibrium; constant straight-line motion with zero net force is dynamic equilibrium.
items.solution_html: Rest with zero net force is static equilibrium; constant straight-line motion with zero net force is dynamic equilibrium.

items.primary_i_can: I can recognize static equilibrium and dynamic equilibrium.
items.evidence_job: Use force and motion evidence together to identify equilibrium.
items.source_basis: Original Unit 1 Assessment Plan §1.4: static/dynamic equilibrium, forces at rest, ΣF=0 for constant straight-line motion; Physics Framework: balanced-force model reasoning.
items.student_text: A cart moves left at constant 3 m/s. Diagram: 25 N ← [cart] → 25 N. Explain why the force and motion evidence are consistent with equilibrium.
items.student_html: A cart moves left at constant 3 m/s. Diagram: 25 N ← [cart] → 25 N. Explain why the force and motion evidence are consistent with equilibrium.
items.answer: The forces balance to zero net force, so constant straight-line velocity can continue.
items.solution_text: Equilibrium means ΣF = 0, not necessarily zero velocity.
items.solution_html: Equilibrium means ΣF = 0, not necessarily zero velocity.

items.primary_i_can: I can explain why an object at rest can still have forces acting on it.
items.evidence_job: Show the real forces acting on an object at rest.
items.source_basis: Original Unit 1 Assessment Plan §1.4: static/dynamic equilibrium, forces at rest, ΣF=0 for constant straight-line motion; Physics Framework: balanced-force model reasoning.
items.student_text: A 75 N crate is at rest on a floor. Draw its vertical force diagram.
items.student_html: A 75 N crate is at rest on a floor. Draw its vertical force diagram.
items.answer: 75 N support upward and 75 N weight downward
items.solution_text: At rest with no vertical acceleration, the upward and downward forces balance.
items.solution_html: At rest with no vertical acceleration, the upward and downward forces balance.

items.primary_i_can: I can explain why an object at rest can still have forces acting on it.
items.evidence_job: Correct the idea that rest means forces disappear.
items.source_basis: Original Unit 1 Assessment Plan §1.4: static/dynamic equilibrium, forces at rest, ΣF=0 for constant straight-line motion; Physics Framework: balanced-force model reasoning.
items.student_text: A student says, “The lamp is at rest, so no forces act on it.” Correct the statement.
items.student_html: A student says, “The lamp is at rest, so no forces act on it.” Correct the statement.
items.answer: Weight acts downward and support/tension acts upward; the forces balance to zero net force.
items.solution_text: Equilibrium can contain multiple real forces whose vector sum is zero.
items.solution_html: Equilibrium can contain multiple real forces whose vector sum is zero.

items.evidence_job: Explain constant straight-line motion as compatible with equilibrium.
items.source_basis: Original Unit 1 Assessment Plan §1.4: static/dynamic equilibrium, forces at rest, ΣF=0 for constant straight-line motion; Physics Framework: balanced-force model reasoning.
items.student_text: A cart travels straight at constant speed. Why can it be in equilibrium while moving?
items.student_html: A cart travels straight at constant speed. Why can it be in equilibrium while moving?
items.answer: Because equilibrium requires zero net force and therefore constant velocity, not necessarily rest.
items.solution_text: Dynamic equilibrium is the moving case of zero net force.
items.solution_html: Dynamic equilibrium is the moving case of zero net force.
